newsitem.title: UK: N.Irish police foil suspected IRA ambush.
newsitem.headline: N.Irish police foil suspected IRA ambush.

text.p: Northern Irish police foiled a suspected IRA guerrilla ambush and arrested one person in south Belfast on Wednesday, security sources said.

Police seized two loaded assault rifles when they raided a house that had been taken over by armed men. The sources said the Irish Republican Army, which is fighting to end rule from Britain, was thought to be behind the incident.
"It is clear that this was a determined attempt by terrorists to kill or maim," Belfast police commander Bill Stewart said in a statement.
"We consider the recovery of two AK-47 rifles which were fully loaded and ready for use to be very significant indeed. It is clear lives have been saved today..."
He said that one person had been arrested for questioning.
The attempted ambush was in Black's Road, near Dunmurry, which is often used by patrolling British army and police vehicles en route to a nearby Irish nationalist area.
Security analysts said AK-47s have frequently been used by IRA fighters in security force ambushes.
Police said that they were alerted to the incident by "suspicious activity" in the area.
It happened just hours ahead of a major parliamentary statement by British Prime Minister Tony Blair aimed at getting the IRA to call an end to its violence to win a political voice in peace talks.
Blair told the British House of Commons of Anglo-Irish plans for resolving a long-running deadlock over how to achieve IRA disarmament if the guerrillas called a truce.
He said the IRA must unequivocally abandon violence before its Sinn Fein political wing is given a seat in all-party talks.
